idiom_name: Transform streams (objectMode) + stream.pipeline for wiring and error propagation
implementation_notes: In Node.js the pattern's roles are concrete: a filter is a Transform stream implementing _transform(chunk, enc, cb), the pipe is the stream's internal buffer between stages, and stream.pipeline(...stages, cb) wires them, propagates errors and destroys the chain on failure. Backpressure is automatic - write() returns false past highWaterMark and the upstream pipe pauses - which is why streams remain the default for byte- and record-oriented Node pipelines. Use objectMode for record pipelines and async generator functions when a stage reads more naturally as a loop than as a class.
pitfalls: A _transform that never calls cb() stalls the stream forever, and calling it twice throws ERR_MULTIPLE_CALLBACK.
Stages must honour the callback error protocol; a stage that swallows errors or bypasses pipeline() leaves listeners, file handles and sockets open when the chain fails.
highWaterMark counts objects in objectMode and bytes otherwise, so a byte-based watermark on an object stream gives no meaningful bound.

variants.name: Async generator stages consumed with for await...of
variants.idiom_name: async function* stages composed by nesting, pulled with for await...of
variants.implementation_notes: Async generators make a stage an ordinary async loop: each generator consumes an async iterable with for await...of and yields transformed records, so a pipeline is composition of functions (stage3(stage2(source()))) with no stream classes and no callback discipline; backpressure is inherent because the consumer awaits each step. Node's stream.pipeline() accepts async generators directly, so the same stages can join a stream chain when byte streams or multiple consumers are involved. Choose generators for readable sequential logic and streams when you need typed byte handling, chunking or highWaterMark buffering.
pitfalls: Breaking out of a for await...of loop early closes the generator, so cleanup must live in finally blocks or the source file/socket leaks.
An async generator is single-use: iterating it again yields nothing, unlike an array-backed chain that can be replayed.
